# Writing characters and booleans

How characters, character slices and booleans render, and how a value that is no character is escaped.

<h2 id="replacement-character"><code>ReplacementCharacter</code></h2>

```rux
pub const ReplacementCharacter: char32 = 0xFFFDu32 as char32;
```

The character written in place of anything that is not one.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/Char8.rux#L12)

<h2 id="maximum-scalar-value"><code>MaximumScalarValue</code></h2>

```rux
pub const MaximumScalarValue: uint64 = 0x10FFFF;
```

The largest value a Unicode scalar can have, past which nothing is a character.
Named because a `char64` has room for a great deal more than this, and the check that it does not hold one has
to happen at the full width: narrowing first would turn `0x100000041` into `A`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/CharacterText.rux#L25)

<h2 id="is-wide-scalar-value"><code>IsWideScalarValue</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsWideScalarValue(value: uint64) -> bool
```

Whether `value`, at whatever width it was read from, is a Unicode scalar value.
Takes a `uint64` so that a `char64` is checked before it is narrowed rather than after. A value past the last
scalar and a value in the surrogate range are both refused, which is the same rule `Text::IsScalarValue`
applies at thirty-two bits.
Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/CharacterText.rux#L35)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type     | Description                                        |
| ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `value` | `uint64` | the numeric value of a character, at its own width |

**Returns**: true when a character of that value exists

<h2 id="write-invalid-escape"><code>WriteInvalidEscape</code></h2>

```rux
pub func WriteInvalidEscape(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    value: uint64
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the escape for a value that is not a character, preserving exactly what it was.
A value that fits a byte is written `\x{nn}`, because a stray byte is not a scalar and should not be shown as
one; anything else is written `\u{...}` with as many digits as its width needs, in fours. No valid character
can collide with either: the escapes are only ever written for values that are not characters.
Reports whatever the writer reported, stopping at the first refusal.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/CharacterText.rux#L60)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                |
| -------- | ----------------- | -------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination            |
| `value`  | `uint64`          | the numeric value to spell |

**Returns**: success when the whole escape was accepted

<h2 id="write-character-debug"><code>WriteCharacterDebug</code></h2>

```rux
pub func WriteCharacterDebug(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    value: uint64,
    whole: bool
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes one character's `Debug` form: quoted, and preserved exactly when it is not a character.
`whole` is the caller's own answer to whether the value is a whole character, because the widths disagree about
it. A `char8` of 0xC3 is a valid scalar value as a number and a piece of a character as a byte, and it is the
byte's answer that governs: `Display` writes U+FFFD for it, so `Debug` must preserve the byte rather than write
the character that number happens to name.
Reports whatever the writer reported, stopping at the first refusal.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/CharacterText.rux#L85)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                                                       |
| -------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                                                   |
| `value`  | `uint64`          | the numeric value of the character, at its own width              |
| `whole`  | `bool`            | whether the width this value came from calls it a whole character |

**Returns**: success when the whole rendering was accepted

<h2 id="write-escaped-scalar"><code>WriteEscapedScalar</code></h2>

```rux
pub func WriteEscapedScalar(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    scalar: uint32
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes one scalar as it appears inside a quoted rendering, escaping what would otherwise be ambiguous.
The quote, the backslash and the control characters get the escapes `Rux/Text` gives them everywhere else, so a
quoted character reads the same here as inside a quoted string.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `TextFailure(InvalidUtf8)` for a value that is not a scalar, which a
caller checks before calling.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/CharacterText.rux#L105)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                       |
| -------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                   |
| `scalar` | `uint32`          | the Unicode scalar value to write |

**Returns**: success when the whole character was accepted

<h2 id="measure-padding"><code>MeasurePadding</code></h2>

```rux
pub func MeasurePadding(
    spec: FormatSpec,
    occupied: uint,
    before: *var uint,
    after: *var uint
)
```

Reports how much fill a spec asks for on each side of a rendering `occupied` characters wide.
A character slice cannot hand its rendering to `WriteAligned`, because the bytes do not exist until they are
transcoded and transcoding into a buffer would bound how long a slice may be. So the width is measured in one
pass over the units and the fill is written around the transcoding instead. Both counts are zero when the
rendering already fills the width, which is the common case and costs nothing.
Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/CharacterText.rux#L130)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type         | Description                                   |
| ---------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `spec`     | `FormatSpec` | what the placeholder asked for                |
| `occupied` | `uint`       | how many characters the rendering will occupy |
| `before`   | `*var uint`  | receives the fill to write first              |
| `after`    | `*var uint`  | receives the fill to write last               |

<h2 id="format-scalar"><code>FormatScalar</code></h2>

```rux
pub func FormatScalar(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec,
    scalar: char32
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes one character under `spec`'s width, fill and alignment.
Reports `TextFailure(InvalidUtf8)` when `scalar` is not a Unicode scalar value, and otherwise whatever the
writer reported.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/IntegerText.rux#L116)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                        |
| -------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                    |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for     |
| `scalar` | `char32`          | the Unicode scalar value to render |

**Returns**: success when the padded character was accepted
